title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 1 diabetes.

HPI
The patient is a known case of type 1 diabetes mellitus presenting for a routine clinic visit. They report stable blood glucose levels and have been adherent to their current regimen. The patient has been managed with insulin long-term and currently takes no oral diabetes medication. They report no acute issues or concerns since the last visit.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term)

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Skin is intact with no signs of infection. Vital signs are stable.

Assessment
The patient has type 1 diabetes mellitus with no complications at this time.

Plan
Continue the current insulin regimen as prescribed. The patient will continue to monitor blood glucose levels and return to the clinic in three months for a follow-up evaluation.
explanations: No complication documented: type 1 diabetes without complications.
Do not assign Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes; insulin use is inherent.

distractors.why: No hyperglycemia or poor control is documented.
Z79.4 is not assigned for type 1 diabetes.
